color.description: Any CSS colour: #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(), hsl(), oklch(). Opaque colours read best; a translucent one is measured over the background of the same mode.

role.description: What the token paints in the sample screen. background: the page. surface: cards and the top bar. surface-muted: table heads and quiet panels. border: dividers. border-strong: input outlines. text, text-muted: body and secondary text. primary / on-primary: the main button, links, the active tab, and the text on that button. accent / on-accent: badges and the avatar. success, warning, danger, info: status messages. focus: the focus ring.

notes.description: Markdown: what this round is, and what to look at.

name.description: The product the palettes are for. The sample screen shows it in its top bar.

description.description: A line on the product and the feel it is after.

checks.description: Contrast pairs to measure beside the standard ones, in every palette that has both tokens.

fg.description: The foreground: a token's name, or a role.

bg.description: The background: a token's name, or a role.

min.description: The least ratio that passes. Default 4.5, WCAG AA for body text; 3 for large text and UI parts.

reasoning.description: Markdown: the idea behind the palette.

tokens.description: The palette's colour tokens, in the order to list them. The five roles background, surface, text, primary and on-primary must each be played by one token.

name.description: The token's name as your code knows it, e.g. color.primary or --brand-500. Comments and edits come back by this name.

light.description: The value in the light theme.

dark.description: The value in the dark theme.

value.description: One value for both themes, instead of light and dark.
